levorotatory: (of an optically active compound or crystal) That rotates the plane of polarized light to the left, or counter-clockwise.
levulin: A substance resembling dextrin, obtained from the bulbs of the dahlia, the artichoke, and other sources, that yields levulose on decomposition.
levulose: D-fructose, the left-rotating stereoisomer of fructose.
levy: To impose (a tax or fine) to collect monies due, or to confiscate property.
levying: present participle and gerund of levy
lewder: comparative form of lewd: more lewd
lewdest: superlative form of lewd: most lewd
lewdness: The quality, state or instance of being lewd; promiscuous.
lewis: A cramp iron inserted into a cavity in order to lift heavy stones; used as a symbol of strength in Freemasonry.
lewisite: An organoarsenic compound used as a chemical weapon.
lewisson: A cramp iron inserted into a cavity in order to lift heavy stones.
lex: To perform lexical analysis; to convert a character stream to a token stream as a preliminary to parsing.
lexeme: A lexical item corresponding to the set of all words (or of all multi-word expressions) that are semantically related through inflection of a particular shared basic form.
lexemic: Of or relating to a lexeme.
lexical: Concerning the vocabulary, words, sentences or morphemes of a language.
lexicalization: The act or process of lexicalizing.
lexicalize: To become part of the vocabulary of a language as a single lexical unit with a distinct meaning.
lexicalized: simple past and past participle of lexicalize
lexicalizes: third-person singular simple present indicative of lexicalize
lexicalizing: present participle and gerund of lexicalize
lexicographer: One who writes or compiles a dictionary.
lexicographic: Like a dictionary, relating to lexicography (the writing of a dictionary).
lexicography: The art or craft of compiling, writing, and editing dictionaries.
lexicology: The part of linguistics that studies words, their nature and meaning, words' elements, relations between words including semantic relations, words groups and the whole lexicon.
lexis: The set of all words and phrases in a language; any unified subset of words from a particular language.
ley: Arable land used temporarily for hay or grazing.
